questions.prompt: Which challenges does OpenAI's guide list for an LLM judge?

options.text: Low recall on long inputs, and a habit of giving every output the same middle score
options.explanation: The guide does not list these. It names position bias and verbosity bias.

options.text: Position bias, which follows reply order, and verbosity bias, which favours long replies
options.explanation: Right. These are the two challenges named in the guide.

options.text: The judge is always too expensive to use on more than a handful of test outputs or so
options.explanation: The guide calls model judges cheaper to run and more scalable than human evaluation.

questions.prompt: What does Claude's guide say to do with LLM-based grading before you use it at scale?

options.text: Test that it is reliable first, and only after that scale it up for the whole set
options.explanation: Right. The guide says: test to ensure reliability first, then scale.

options.text: Scale it first, since the large number of grades will average out any single mistake
options.explanation: The guide says to test reliability first. Many grades repeat a bias; they do not cancel it.

options.text: Replace it with human grading, since the guide says humans are fast and cheap enough
options.explanation: The guide calls human grading slow and expensive, and says to avoid it if possible.

questions.prompt: How does the Anthropic engineering post suggest you avoid made-up verdicts from a judge model?

options.text: Ask the judge to answer much faster, so that it has less time to guess at an answer
options.explanation: The post gives no such advice. It suggests an instruction to return Unknown.

options.text: Give it a way out: an instruction to return "Unknown" when it lacks information
options.explanation: Right. This is the post's own example of a way out.

options.text: Hide the rubric from the judge, so it cannot write a verdict that just fits the rubric
options.explanation: The post asks for clear, structured rubrics. A hidden rubric would remove the guide for the judge.
